stories.headline: Apple Officially Approves Tiny Corp Driver Enabling Nvidia and AMD eGPUs on Apple Silicon Macs

key_facts.fact: Apple signed Tiny Corp's TinyGPU driver extension, enabling AMD and Nvidia eGPUs to work on Apple Silicon Macs over Thunderbolt/USB4 without disabling System Integrity Protection.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple has signed a driver for AMD or Nvidia eGPUs connected to Apple Silicon but there are some big caveats, and it won't improve your graphics.

key_facts.fact: The driver is designed for AI research and LLM inference, not gaming or graphics acceleration. Video to an external monitor is not accelerated.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple approved drivers enabling AMD and Nvidia external GPUs to function on Mac systems. However, the software is specifically designed for AI applications rather than gaming purposes.

key_facts.fact: A Mac mini M4 with a Radeon RX 7900 XTX via Thunderbolt/USB4 achieved 18.5 tokens per second running Qwen 3.5 27B, a 27-billion-parameter language model.
key_facts.excerpt: A Mac mini with an M4 chip connected to a Radeon RX 7900 XTX via Thunderbolt/USB4 achieved 18.5 tokens per second running Qwen 3.5 27B.

key_facts.fact: Supported GPUs require AMD RDNA3+ or Nvidia Ampere+ at minimum, with macOS 12.1 or later and a Thunderbolt 3/USB4 port.
key_facts.excerpt: It requires a Mac running macOS 12.1 or later, a spare USB4 or Thunderbolt 3 port or newer, and a supported GPU with an enclosure that delivers sufficient power.

key_facts.fact: This marks the first time macOS has supported third-party discrete GPUs on Apple Silicon through an officially sanctioned mechanism, after more than a year of Tiny Corp engineering custom userspace GPU drivers.
key_facts.excerpt: After more than a year of engineering custom userspace GPU drivers, the approval marks the first time macOS has supported third-party discrete GPUs on Apple Silicon through an officially sanctioned mechanism.

stories.headline: Planet Labs Indefinitely Withholds Iran Conflict Satellite Imagery at US Government Request

key_facts.fact: Planet Labs announced it will indefinitely withhold satellite imagery of Iran and the conflict region after the US government asked all satellite imagery providers to restrict access.
key_facts.excerpt: Satellite imaging firm Planet Labs said on Saturday it will indefinitely withhold visuals of Iran and the region of conflict.

key_facts.fact: The restriction applies retroactively from March 9 and is expected to remain in place until the conflict ends. It expands upon a 14-day delay on imagery Planet Labs imposed last month.
key_facts.excerpt: The measures would apply retroactively from March 9 and are expected to remain in place until the conflict ends.

key_facts.fact: Planet Labs will switch to a managed distribution system, releasing imagery on a case-by-case basis for urgent, mission-critical requirements or in the public interest.
key_facts.excerpt: Planet Labs will release imagery on a case-by-case basis for urgent, mission-critical requirements or in the public interest.

key_facts.fact: The announcement was made via email to Planet Labs customers, noting the US government had asked all satellite imagery providers to cooperate.
key_facts.excerpt: US satellite firm Planet Labs announces blackout on war on Iran images.

stories.headline: Artemis II Crew Completes First Manual Piloting of Orion Spacecraft in Deep Space

key_facts.fact: NASA astronaut Christina Koch and CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen manually piloted the Orion spacecraft for 41 minutes starting at 9:09 p.m. EDT on Flight Day 4, testing six-degrees-of-freedom and three-degrees-of-freedom thruster modes.
key_facts.excerpt: Koch and Hansen took turns controlling the spacecraft starting at 9:09 p.m. EDT. For 41 minutes, the pair tested two different thruster modes, six degrees of freedom and three degrees of freedom.

key_facts.fact: At wakeup on Flight Day 4, Orion was approximately 169,000 miles from Earth with the Moon at 110,700 miles, as the crew prepared for the lunar flyby scheduled for April 6.
key_facts.excerpt: At wakeup on flight day 4, the spacecraft and its crew were approximately 169,000 miles from Earth and approaching the Moon at 110,700 miles.

key_facts.fact: The crew reviewed lunar surface features selected by NASA's science team for observation during their six-hour flyby, which begins at 2:45 p.m. on April 6 when cabin windows will point toward the Moon.
key_facts.excerpt: After the piloting demonstration, the crew reviewed a list of the surface features the NASA science team had asked them to analyze and photograph during their six-hour flyby.

key_facts.fact: The crew captured the first-ever human-eye views of the Orientale basin, a 930 km multi-ringed impact crater on the Moon's far side that scientists use as an archetype for understanding impact basins across the solar system.
key_facts.excerpt: Artemis II shares new images as it gets closer to the moon.

key_facts.fact: Commander Reid Wiseman and Pilot Victor Glover will repeat the manual piloting demonstration on Flight Day 8 (April 9) to gather additional spacecraft performance data.
key_facts.excerpt: Wiseman and Glover will repeat the demonstration on Flight Day 8 (April 9).

stories.headline: Nearly Half of Planned US Data Center Builds Delayed or Canceled Over Power and Supply Shortages

key_facts.fact: Close to half of planned US data center builds this year are projected to be delayed or canceled, despite unprecedented levels of AI infrastructure investment.
key_facts.excerpt: Half of planned US data center builds have been delayed or canceled, growth limited by shortages of power infrastructure and parts from China.

key_facts.fact: Imports of high-power transformers from China surged from fewer than 1,500 units in 2022 to more than 8,000 units in 2025, highlighting dependence on Chinese electrical equipment manufacturing.
key_facts.excerpt: Imports of high-power transformers from China surged from fewer than 1,500 units in 2022 to more than 8,000 units in 2025.

key_facts.fact: Among data centers slated for 2027, only 6.3 GW of computing infrastructure is under construction versus 21.5 GW announced, with the vast majority planned for 2028-2032 not yet having broken ground.
key_facts.excerpt: Among data centers slated to open in 2027, only about 6.3 gigawatts worth of computing infrastructure are actually under construction compared to 21.5 announced gigawatts.

key_facts.fact: The six largest US hyperscalers are projected to spend approximately $700 billion this year on data center capex, nearly six times 2022 levels, according to Moody's Ratings.
key_facts.excerpt: Six largest US hyperscalers projected to spend approximately $700 billion this year—nearly six times 2022 levels.

stories.headline: SpaceX Starship V3 First Flight Slips From April to May as Vehicle Integration Continues

key_facts.fact: Elon Musk confirmed on X that the next Starship launch (Flight 12, the first V3 flight) is 4-6 weeks away, placing the window in early to mid-May 2026, after previously targeting late April.
key_facts.excerpt: Elon Musk reveals next Starship launch planned for May 2026.

key_facts.fact: Flight 12 will be the first flight of V3 hardware, a ground-up redesign stacking Booster 19 with Ship 39, featuring increased propellant capacity and more powerful Raptor 3 engines.
key_facts.excerpt: Starship Flight 12 will be the first flight of Version 3 (V3) hardware—a ground-up redesign. The vehicle stacks Booster 19 with Ship 39.

key_facts.fact: The V3 Starship can deliver more than 100 tons to low Earth orbit, roughly three times what V2 managed, with some estimates putting the theoretical ceiling near 200 tons with full reusability.
key_facts.excerpt: More than 100 tons to low Earth orbit is roughly three times what V2 could manage—and some estimates put the theoretical ceiling closer to 200 tons with full reusability factored in.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX fired up the V3 Starship for the first time in March ahead of the planned launch, as the company packed dozens of upgrades into the vehicle for reliability and NASA Artemis suitability.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX fires up next-gen V3 Starship for 1st time ahead of April launch.

stories.headline: Bipartisan MATCH Act Targets Ban on DUV Lithography Equipment Sales and Servicing to China

key_facts.fact: The Multilateral Alignment of Technology Controls on Hardware (MATCH) Act was introduced in the US House on April 2, with a Senate version being prepared by Senators Pete Ricketts (R-NE) and Andy Kim (D-NJ).
key_facts.excerpt: Bill to ban sale of key AI chipmaking equipment to China introduced in House.

key_facts.fact: The bill would ban both the sale and servicing of DUV immersion lithography equipment to China's leading chipmakers SMIC, Hua Hong, Huawei, CXMT, and YMTC, extending beyond existing EUV-only restrictions.
key_facts.excerpt: Washington now plans to impose tougher restrictions on ASML's DUV business and its services to China's chip factories.

key_facts.fact: ASML is directly affected as the monopoly provider of advanced lithography equipment; China accounted for 33% of ASML's revenue in 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: In 2025, China accounted for 33 percent of the Dutch chip machine manufacturer's revenue.

key_facts.fact: If allies don't adopt equivalent restrictions, the bill directs Commerce to invoke the foreign direct product rule to force compliance, asserting US jurisdiction over items made with American technology abroad.
key_facts.excerpt: The foreign direct product rule allows the Commerce Department to assert that its export control regulations apply to items manufactured in foreign countries when those items are the direct product of U.S.-made technology.

stories.headline: Intel Pays $14.2B to Buy Back Apollo's 49% Stake in Ireland Fab, Regaining Full Control

key_facts.fact: Intel agreed to pay $14.2 billion (cash plus ~$6.5B in new debt) to repurchase the 49% equity stake in Fab 34 in Leixlip, Ireland, that it sold to Apollo Global Management in 2024 for $11.2 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel to repurchase Apollo's stake in Ireland fab for $14.2B.

key_facts.fact: Fab 34 produces chips based on Intel 4 and Intel 3 technologies, including Core Ultra and Xeon 6 processors. Intel expects the deal to boost profit and strengthen its credit profile from 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel Moves to Reclaim Ireland Fab From Apollo in $14.2B Buyback Amid CPU Demand Strength.

key_facts.fact: Intel shares jumped roughly 9% on the announcement, reflecting market confidence in Intel's manufacturing strategy and improved CPU demand.
key_facts.excerpt: Stock Market Today, April 1: Intel Surges on $14.2 Billion Fab Buyback.

key_facts.fact: The buyback price represents a roughly 27% premium over Apollo's original $11.2 billion acquisition cost in 2024.
key_facts.excerpt: Apollo originally acquired the stake for $11.2 billion in 2024.
